books.title: The Jesus Storybook Bible
books.author: Sally Lloyd-Jones
books.blurb: A read-aloud Bible that keeps pointing every story toward Jesus. Jago's pictures carry the pages.

books.title: The Biggest Story Bible Storybook
books.author: Kevin DeYoung
books.blurb: A full storybook Bible with Don Clark's pictures, written to be read aloud across a year.

books.title: The Child's Story Bible
books.author: Catherine F. Vos
books.blurb: A classic continuous retelling of the Bible, meant for reading aloud over many evenings.

books.title: The Action Bible
books.author: Doug Mauss, illustrated by Sergio Cariello
books.blurb: The Bible told as a graphic novel, with Sergio Cariello's comic art. Good for readers who want pictures and action.

books.title: Noah's Ark
books.author: Jerry Pinkney
books.blurb: A Caldecott Medal picture book that retells the Flood with rich paintings.

books.title: Noah's Ark
books.author: Peter Spier
books.blurb: A mostly wordless picture book. Children can tell the story themselves from the drawings.

books.title: The True Story of Noah's Ark
books.author: Tom Dooley
books.blurb: A picture-book account from a Christian publisher, illustrated by Bill Looney, that treats the ark as real history.
books.parentNote: Written to teach a creationist reading of Genesis. Pair it with the Scripture marker, which is the source.

books.title: Adam and His Kin
books.author: Ruth Beechick
books.blurb: A story woven through the long genealogies from Adam toward Abraham.
books.parentNote: The conversations and daily details are imagined. The Bible is the source. Read it as fiction beside Genesis, not instead of it.

books.title: Life in the Great Ice Age
books.author: Michael J. Oard and Beverly Oard
books.blurb: A children's picture book about a cold age after the Flood, from a creationist point of view.
books.parentNote: This is the interpretation on the ice-age marker, not a claim the Bible describes an ice age.

books.title: Gilgamesh the Hero
books.author: Geraldine McCaughrean
books.blurb: A children's retelling of the ancient Mesopotamian epic.
books.parentNote: This is a legend from Sumer's world, not Scripture and not a history report.

books.title: The Golden Bull
books.author: Marjorie Cowley
books.blurb: Two children in ancient Mesopotamia get caught in a goldsmith's trouble. A story of that world, not a retelling of Abraham.

books.title: Joseph
books.author: Brian Wildsmith
books.blurb: A picture-book retelling of Joseph's life, from the colorful coat to forgiveness in Egypt.

books.title: Exodus
books.author: Brian Wildsmith
books.blurb: A picture-book retelling of the leaving of Egypt, with Wildsmith's bright paintings.

books.title: Tirzah
books.author: Lucille Travis
books.blurb: A novel about a Hebrew girl living as a slave in Egypt at the time of the Exodus.
books.parentNote: The biblical events are the frame. Tirzah's daily scenes are fiction.

books.title: The Golden Goblet
books.author: Eloise Jarvis McGraw
books.blurb: Ranofer, a boy in ancient Egypt, wants to be a goldsmith and uncovers a tomb robbery.

books.title: Mara, Daughter of the Nile
books.author: Eloise Jarvis McGraw
books.blurb: A servant girl carries secret messages in the court of Hatshepsut.
books.parentNote: Adventure and a mild romance. Best for about age 10 and up. It is a novel, not a source for naming the Exodus pharaoh.

books.title: Pyramid
books.author: David Macaulay
books.blurb: Careful drawings that show how a pyramid could be planned and built. One of the best children's books on the subject.

books.title: The Pharaohs of Ancient Egypt
books.author: Elizabeth Payne
books.blurb: A Landmark history that walks through Egypt's rulers for middle-grade readers.
books.parentNote: Uses ordinary textbook dates. Read it next to the timeline's date notes, especially on the pyramids.

books.title: Mummies Made in Egypt
books.author: Aliki
books.blurb: A clear picture book about how and why Egyptians prepared mummies.

books.title: Who Was King Tut?
books.author: Roberta Edwards
books.blurb: A short biography of the boy pharaoh and of the 1922 discovery of his tomb.

books.title: Seeker of Knowledge
books.author: James Rumford
books.blurb: How Jean-Francois Champollion deciphered hieroglyphs in the 1800s, which is how we read Egypt's own writing.

books.title: Mummies in the Morning
books.author: Mary Pope Osborne
books.blurb: Jack and Annie, in the Magic Tree House, take a fantasy trip to ancient Egypt.
books.parentNote: Time-travel fantasy, not a history book. Pair it with the nonfiction companion if you want the facts.

books.title: Mummies and Pyramids
books.author: Will Osborne and Mary Pope Osborne
books.blurb: The nonfiction companion to Mummies in the Morning, with mummies, pyramids, and daily life.
books.parentNote: Uses standard museum dates. Keep the timeline's pyramid note beside it.

books.title: The Cat of Bubastes
books.author: G. A. Henty
books.blurb: A Victorian adventure set in Egypt in the days of Moses, about a sacred cat and an Israelite family.
books.parentNote: Nineteenth-century style, slow for some readers. Henty imagines Egypt in Moses' time. It is not evidence for a date or a pharaoh.

books.title: Casting the Gods Adrift
books.author: Geraldine McCaughrean
books.blurb: A boy in Akhenaten's court watches the pharaoh's strange new worship of the sun disk.

books.title: Hittite Warrior
books.author: Joanne Williamson
books.blurb: A young Hittite flees a falling kingdom and ends up in Canaan in the days of Joshua.
books.parentNote: Historical fiction. The Hittites and the biblical setting are real. The hero's plot is invented.

books.title: God King: A Story in the Days of King Hezekiah
books.author: Joanne Williamson
books.blurb: A prince of Kush is swept into Judah during the days of Hezekiah and the Assyrian threat.
books.parentNote: A novel. Hezekiah, Isaiah, and the Assyrian invasion are the historical frame.

books.title: The Story of the World, Volume 1: Ancient Times
books.author: Susan Wise Bauer
books.blurb: A wide read-aloud history of the ancient world, from early cities through Rome.
books.parentNote: A survey many families read aloud. It is not the Bible, and it does not follow this timeline's creationist chronology. Keep the Scripture, Historical, and Interpretation badges beside it.

books.title: The Story of the World, Volume 2: The Middle Ages
books.author: Susan Wise Bauer
books.blurb: The middle-ages volume of Bauer's read-aloud history, from the fall of Rome toward the Renaissance.
books.parentNote: A wide survey, not a church catechism. Read it next to the timeline's badges.

books.title: The Story of the World, Volume 3: Early Modern Times
books.author: Susan Wise Bauer
books.blurb: Bauer's survey from the age of printing and exploration through the revolutionary era.
books.parentNote: A wide survey. Use the timeline when you want Scripture and history kept distinct.

books.title: The Story of the World, Volume 4: The Modern Age
books.author: Susan Wise Bauer
books.blurb: The modern volume of the read-aloud history, including the world wars.
books.parentNote: War chapters are serious. Read them with a parent. This is a survey, not a memoir like The Hiding Place.

books.title: D'Aulaires' Book of Greek Myths
books.author: Ingri d'Aulaire and Edgar Parin d'Aulaire
books.blurb: The standard children's retelling of the Greek myths, with the d'Aulaires' pictures.
books.parentNote: These are myths, not history and not Scripture. A few stories include jealousy, revenge, and gods behaving badly. This retelling is written for children.

books.title: Black Ships Before Troy
books.author: Rosemary Sutcliff
books.blurb: A strong children's retelling of the Iliad.
books.parentNote: Poetry and legend, not a history book. War and revenge are part of the story.

books.title: Famous Men of Greece
books.author: John H. Haaren and A. B. Poland
books.blurb: Short life stories of Greek figures, written for children in 1904.
books.parentNote: Old-fashioned and clear. It sometimes treats legends as moral tales. Use the timeline badges so myth and history stay distinct.

books.title: Famous Men of Rome
books.author: John H. Haaren and A. B. Poland
books.blurb: Short life stories of Roman figures, a companion to Famous Men of Greece.
books.parentNote: Written in 1904. Early chapters include legends such as Romulus. Later lives are historical.

books.title: Detectives in Togas
books.author: Henry Winterfeld
books.blurb: Schoolboys in ancient Rome solve a mystery. A light adventure, not a history lesson.

books.title: The Bronze Bow
books.author: Elizabeth George Speare
books.blurb: A Newbery Medal novel about a Galilean boy who hates Rome and meets Jesus.
books.parentNote: Includes hatred, grief, and violence in an occupied country. One of the best older-child novels set in Jesus' lifetime.

books.title: The Eagle of the Ninth
books.author: Rosemary Sutcliff
books.blurb: A young Roman officer goes north of Hadrian's Wall to recover a lost eagle standard.
books.parentNote: Battles and a hard journey. Best for older readers. The legion is historical. The plot is fiction. Linked here as a Rome novel.

books.title: Augustus Caesar's World
books.author: Genevieve Foster
books.blurb: Foster tells Augustus's lifetime by also introducing other people alive then, including in Judea.

books.title: Twice Freed
books.author: Patricia St. John
books.blurb: A novel about Onesimus, the enslaved man in Paul's letter to Philemon.
books.parentNote: The letter is Scripture. This book imagines the life around it.

books.title: Victory on the Walls
books.author: Frieda Clark Hyman
books.blurb: A story of a boy in Jerusalem while Nehemiah rebuilds the walls.
books.parentNote: Nehemiah is Scripture. The boy's plot is fiction.

books.title: Adam of the Road
books.author: Elizabeth Janet Gray
books.blurb: A Newbery Medal novel about a minstrel's son on the roads of thirteenth-century England.

books.title: The Door in the Wall
books.author: Marguerite de Angeli
books.blurb: A Newbery Medal story of a boy in medieval England who loses the use of his legs and finds another kind of strength.

books.title: Castle
books.author: David Macaulay
books.blurb: How a thirteenth-century castle in Wales could be built, drawn step by step.

books.title: Cathedral
books.author: David Macaulay
books.blurb: How a Gothic cathedral could be raised over decades, with Macaulay's famous drawings.

books.title: Otto of the Silver Hand
books.author: Howard Pyle
books.blurb: A nineteenth-century story of a gentle boy raised in a monastery and caught in a robber baron's feud.
books.parentNote: Includes a violent injury: a boy's hand is cut off. Better for older children.

books.title: Augustine Came to Kent
books.author: Barbara Willard
books.blurb: A novel about the mission to the English in 597. This Augustine is not Augustine of Hippo.

books.title: Son of Charlemagne
books.author: Barbara Willard
books.blurb: A novel about Charlemagne's son in the emperor's court.

books.title: If All the Swords in England
books.author: Barbara Willard
books.blurb: A story of two brothers on opposite sides of the quarrel that ends in Becket's murder.
books.parentNote: The killing in the cathedral is part of the plot. For older children.

books.title: Viking Ships at Sunrise
books.author: Mary Pope Osborne
books.blurb: A Magic Tree House fantasy visit to a monastery in the time of Viking raids.
books.parentNote: Time-travel fiction, not a history of the Vikings.

books.title: When Lightning Struck!: The Story of Martin Luther
books.author: Danika Cooley
books.blurb: A children's biography of Luther from a Christian writer.

books.title: Martin Luther: A Man Who Changed the World
books.author: Paul L. Maier
books.blurb: A picture-book biography of Luther for younger listeners.

books.title: Thunderstorm in Church
books.author: Louise A. Vernon
books.blurb: A story told through Luther's son, set in the reformer's busy household.
books.parentNote: Historical fiction. The family details are imagined around a real man.

books.title: Ink on His Fingers
books.author: Louise A. Vernon
books.blurb: A boy's-eye view of Gutenberg's print shop.
books.parentNote: Fiction set in a real workshop.

books.title: The Bible Smuggler
books.author: Louise A. Vernon
books.blurb: A story of William Tyndale's English New Testament being carried into England.
books.parentNote: Fiction built around Tyndale's real work and danger.

books.title: The Hawk That Dare Not Hunt by Day
books.author: Scott O'Dell
books.blurb: A novel about a young sailor who helps smuggle Tyndale's Scriptures.
books.parentNote: O'Dell writes for older children. The danger around Tyndale is real. The sailor's plot is fiction.

books.title: The World of Columbus and Sons
books.author: Genevieve Foster
books.blurb: Foster's wide look at the people alive in Columbus's era, not only Columbus.

books.title: Around the World in a Hundred Years
books.author: Jean Fritz
books.blurb: Short, lively chapters on explorers from Henry the Navigator to Magellan.
books.parentNote: Fritz is honest and sometimes wry about the explorers' mistakes and cruelties. Good to read with a parent.

books.title: Pedro's Journal
books.author: Pam Conrad
books.blurb: A short fictional journal of a ship's boy on Columbus's first voyage.
books.parentNote: Fiction. Pair it with a conversation about the people who already lived in the Americas.

books.title: Ship
books.author: David Macaulay
books.blurb: How an exploration-age ship was built and sailed, shown in Macaulay's drawings.

books.title: Carry On, Mr. Bowditch
books.author: Jean Lee Latham
books.blurb: A Newbery Medal novel based on the real navigator Nathaniel Bowditch.
books.parentNote: The life is real. The scenes are written as a novel.

books.title: If You Lived in Colonial Times
books.author: Ann McGovern
books.blurb: A question-and-answer picture book about daily life in colonial New England.

books.title: Squanto, Friend of the Pilgrims
books.author: Clyde Robert Bulla
books.blurb: An easy biography of Tisquantum and his help to the Plymouth settlers.
books.parentNote: Written in 1954. It honors Squanto's help. Read it with the harder history that his people suffered greatly from disease and settlement.

books.title: The Courage of Sarah Noble
books.author: Alice Dalgliesh
books.blurb: A short novel based on a real girl who went with her father into the Connecticut woods in 1707.
books.parentNote: Linked with the colonial shelf. Some language about Native people reflects the 1950s, when it was written.

books.title: The Sign of the Beaver
books.author: Elizabeth George Speare
books.blurb: A colonial boy left alone in the Maine woods learns from a Penobscot boy.
books.parentNote: Written in 1983. Some wording for Native people reflects that time. Worth reading with a parent. Placed on the westward shelf as a story of settlement.

books.title: Ben and Me
books.author: Robert Lawson
books.blurb: A humorous novel in which a mouse claims to have given Benjamin Franklin his best ideas.
books.parentNote: A joke, not a biography.

books.title: Johnny Tremain
books.author: Esther Forbes
books.blurb: A Newbery Medal novel about a silversmith's apprentice in Boston at the start of the Revolution.
books.parentNote: Includes war and a bad burn from hot metal. A classic for about age 10 and up.

books.title: George Washington's World
books.author: Genevieve Foster
books.blurb: Washington's lifetime told alongside other people then alive, in Foster's signature style.

books.title: Henry's Freedom Box
books.author: Ellen Levine
books.blurb: A picture book of Henry Brown, who mailed himself to freedom. Illustrated by Kadir Nelson.
books.parentNote: A true story. The danger is clear and not graphic. Good to read with a younger child and talk about.

books.title: Moses: When Harriet Tubman Led Her People to Freedom
books.author: Carole Boston Weatherford
books.blurb: A poetic picture book of Tubman's escape and rescue work, illustrated by Kadir Nelson. The title uses Moses as a picture of her courage.
books.parentNote: It is about Harriet Tubman, not the biblical Moses. Faith is part of the telling.

books.title: Freedom Train: The Story of Harriet Tubman
books.author: Dorothy Sterling
books.blurb: A middle-grade biography of Tubman, including her work in the Civil War.

books.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
books.author: Frederick Douglass
books.blurb: Douglass's own 1845 account of slavery and escape.
books.parentNote: He truthfully describes violence and the evil of slavery. Best for mature readers, with a parent nearby.

books.title: Little House on the Prairie
books.author: Laura Ingalls Wilder
books.blurb: A novel based on the author's childhood in a settler family.
books.parentNote: Told from a settler family's point of view. Some passages reflect unfair attitudes of the 1800s toward Native Americans. Read those pages with a parent.

books.title: The Bobbin Girl
books.author: Emily Arnold McCully
books.blurb: A picture book based on a real mill girl in Lowell who joins a protest.
books.parentNote: The hours and the protest are historically grounded. The girl's scenes are a story.

books.title: Mill
books.author: David Macaulay
books.blurb: How New England mills were planned and built, in Macaulay's illustrated style.

books.title: Ten Mile Day and the Building of the Transcontinental Railroad
books.author: Mary Ann Fraser
books.blurb: The day crews laid ten miles of track, and how the railroad was raced to completion.

books.title: The Great Railroad Race
books.author: Kristiana Gregory
books.blurb: A Dear America diary of a girl in Utah while the transcontinental railroad is being built.
books.parentNote: Fiction in diary form. The railroad setting is historical.

books.title: Number the Stars
books.author: Lois Lowry
books.blurb: A Newbery Medal novel about a Danish girl who helps her Jewish friend hide from the Nazis.
books.parentNote: Set in occupied Denmark. Tension and danger, without graphic violence. Often read around ages 8-12 with a parent nearby.

books.title: Snow Treasure
books.author: Marie McSwigan
books.blurb: A novel about Norwegian children smuggling gold past Nazi soldiers on their sleds.
books.parentNote: Inspired by a wartime story from Norway. Treat the plot as fiction.

books.title: Twenty and Ten
books.author: Claire Huchet Bishop
books.blurb: French schoolchildren hide ten Jewish children from Nazi soldiers. A short, tense, hopeful book.

books.title: The Hiding Place (Young Reader's Edition)
books.author: Corrie ten Boom with Elizabeth and John Sherrill
books.blurb: Corrie ten Boom's account of hiding Jewish neighbors and of the camp that followed, in the edition shortened for younger readers.
books.parentNote: The young reader's edition softens some details. It still describes arrest, camp life, and death. Read it with a parent.
